To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) libraries are using social media in an attempt to market services and connect with young people; (2) libraries are not using social media effectively and are not reaching their potential audience; (3) librarians are using social media for personal reasons rather than professional ones, and are using it as a marketing tool in a limited manner; (4) librarians do not have the time, knowledge or resources to use social media effectively; (5) students are not using library social media accounts
libraries are not currently making use of social media to their full advantage.

libraries are struggling to engage with their users through social media and that the reasons for this are varied, but include the lack of time, resources and knowledge to engage in the activity, the lack of understanding by the library staff as to why social media is an important part of their role, and that the users themselves are not aware of the benefits to them of social media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how libraries are currently marketing themselves on social media, how librarians are using these channels, what they are trying to achieve and how they perceive the effectiveness of these efforts.
the effectiveness of social media in the context of libraries and, in particular, the use of Twitter as a marketing tool in the sector.
the use of Twitter as a marketing tool and its effectiveness in promoting the library as an institution and its services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social media is not a suitable tool for marketing libraries to students, and that libraries should not be encouraged to invest time, effort and resources in this area.
social media has a role in library promotion but it is not the only tool and should not be used in isolation.
social media is not a viable marketing tool for the library in educational institutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the library profession needs to be more aware of the needs of their potential users and the ways in which they are using social media, in order to be able to effectively market their services.
the use of social networks in libraries is still in its infancy and that there is still a lot of work to be done to make them a success.
the library is a place for people to come and learn and to share information and that social media can be an effective tool to achieve that goal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
libraries need to take a more active role in engaging with students on social media and that the use of social networks should not be seen as a one-way communication tool.
social media is not a panacea for all the ills of libraries and, in particular, the marketing of their services to students.
libraries need to be more aware and more responsive to their users, and that social media provides the opportunity to do so, if only libraries are willing to engage in a more user-centred approach.
